markets-finance.title: India Wants Your Dollars. The RBI Is Dusting Off the 2013 Playbook — NRI Bonds, FCNR Deposits, Emergency Swaps — to Stop the Rupee From Hitting 100. If You Have a Dollar Account, You Are About to Be Courted.
markets-finance.excerpt: The Reserve Bank of India conducted a $5 billion dollar-rupee swap auction on May 26, 2026 — the same day the rupee was trading near its record low of 96.96 per dollar. But the swap is only one weapon in an escalating arsenal. Sources familiar with the central bank's thinking told multiple outlets that the RBI is actively evaluating the launch of Foreign Currency Non-Resident (FCNR) deposit schemes, the issuance of NRI bonds, and additional swap operations to mobilise dollar inflows from the Indian diaspora. The last time India took these steps was during the 2013 taper tantrum crisis, when the rupee fell to 68.85 against the dollar and the RBI raised $34 billion from NRIs in three months through FCNR-B deposits offered at subsidised rates. That 2013 operation is widely credited with stabilising the currency and averting a balance-of-payments crisis. India's current predicament is arguably worse: the Iran war has pushed Brent crude above $100 per barrel, foreign portfolio investors have sold $23 billion of Indian equities in 2026, the rupee has fallen 6 percent since January, the RBI is spending an estimated $1 billion per day in the spot market to prevent further collapse, and fuel prices have been hiked four times in May alone — a cumulative increase of ₹7.5 per litre. For the estimated 32 million members of the Indian diaspora — particularly the 4.5 million Indian Americans who hold dollar-denominated savings, earn dollar salaries, and send an estimated $30 billion in remittances to India each year — the coming weeks may present a once-in-a-decade financial decision. The RBI is about to ask you for your dollars. Understanding what FCNR deposits are, how the 2013 scheme worked, what the current remittance and property arbitrage looks like, and whether parking your dollars in India makes financial sense requires more than a headline. It requires context.

technology.title: Anthropic Refused to Let the Pentagon Use Its AI for Mass Surveillance. Now It's Blacklisted.
technology.excerpt: The standoff between the AI safety company and the U.S. Department of Defense — with a May 31 deadline looming — has become the most consequential AI governance fight in years. Indian AI researchers are watching closely.
technology.nri_angle: Anthropic employs a significant number of Indian-origin AI researchers and engineers, many on H-1B visas, who face direct career uncertainty from the standoff. The case also sets precedent for how AI companies can resist government overreach — a question that matters deeply as India drafts its own AI governance framework. For Indian tech workers choosing between AI labs, the ethics-vs-government-contracts tradeoff just became very real.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Lisa Su Says AI Is 'Still in the Third Inning.' AMD Is Betting $10 Billion on It.
technology.excerpt: AMD's chair and CEO commits the company's largest-ever regional investment to Taiwan's semiconductor ecosystem — and warns the global CPU market is 'tight' with no relief in sight.
technology.nri_angle: AMD's India R&D centers in Hyderabad and Bangalore — with over 6,000 engineers — are deeply involved in EPYC server chip development and AI software optimization. Taiwan's supply chain health directly determines whether those engineers' work reaches production on schedule. For NRI investors, Su's 'third inning' thesis means the AI infrastructure buildout has years of runway left.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Nvidia's Vera CPU Is an ARM Chip That Outperforms Intel and AMD. Indian Engineers Helped Build It.
technology.excerpt: The 88-core Olympus processor, purpose-built for agentic AI, has posted benchmark numbers that no ARM chip has ever matched — and thousands of Indian engineers in Bangalore and Pune contributed to its design.
technology.nri_angle: NVIDIA employs thousands of engineers across Bangalore, Pune, and Hyderabad — many of whom contributed to the Vera CPU architecture and its supporting software stack. For Indian chip designers weighing career moves, Vera signals that ARM-based data center processors are no longer a niche bet. And for NRI investors tracking NVIDIA, Vera opens a new $200 billion server CPU market opportunity on top of the GPU business.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Britain Just Told Sunil Mittal He Can't Buy More of BT. Here's Why It Matters.
technology.excerpt: The UK government is blocking India's telecom titan from raising his BT stake beyond 25%, invoking national security over its fibre-optic backbone. For Indian capital eyeing Western infrastructure, the ceiling just got lower.
technology.image_caption: Sunil Bharti Mittal, founder and chairman of Bharti Enterprises. Photo: Wikimedia Commons
technology.nri_angle: Indian billionaire capital being blocked from Western telecom infrastructure raises questions about how Indian investment will be treated globally — relevant to NRI investors, Bharti Airtel shareholders, and anyone watching India's push to become a global business power.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Standard Chartered Is Cutting 7,000 Jobs With AI. Its CEO Called Them 'Lower-Value Human Capital.'
technology.excerpt: The bank plans to eliminate 15% of its back-office roles by 2030, with hubs in Bengaluru and Chennai bearing the heaviest burden. CEO Bill Winters apologised for the phrasing. The layoffs are proceeding anyway.
technology.image_caption: Standard Chartered CEO Bill Winters at the World Economic Forum, 2021. Photo: Wikimedia Commons
technology.nri_angle: Standard Chartered employs tens of thousands in Bengaluru and Chennai back-office hubs — exactly the roles being targeted. For NRI finance professionals and their families in India, this is a direct threat to livelihoods. AI salary inflation of 40-50% in India tech roles means even the survivors face a transformed career landscape.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Synopsys Just Coined the Term 'Agent Engineer.' India's Chip Designers Should Pay Attention.
technology.excerpt: The EDA giant raised its forecast on surging AI chip design demand and struck a deal with activist investor Elliott. Its new pitch: AI 'agent engineers' that work alongside human designers. India's 50,000-strong chip design workforce is directly in the path of this shift.
technology.image_caption: Microchips on a circuit board. AI is reshaping how these are designed. Photo: Pexels
technology.nri_angle: Synopsys employs thousands of engineers in India, its largest non-US engineering hub. India's semiconductor design workforce of ~50,000 engineers is directly affected by the 'agent engineer' concept — AI tools that augment or replace parts of the chip design process. For Indian chip designers in the Bay Area and Bengaluru, this reshapes career trajectories.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Pichai's Alphabet Lands the Biggest AI Deal of the Year — Powering Apple's Siri
technology.excerpt: Apple will pay Google roughly $1 billion a year to run Gemini under the hood of its voice assistant. For Indian-origin tech leaders, it is a full-circle moment.
technology.image_caption: Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet, whose Gemini AI models will power Apple's next-generation Siri. Photo: Wikimedia Commons
technology.nri_angle: Sundar Pichai's Alphabet cements its position as the foundational AI infrastructure provider for 2 billion Apple devices. Indian engineers at both companies are central to the integration, and NRI investors holding both AAPL and GOOGL have reason to pay close attention.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Qualcomm's ByteDance Deal Signals a New Front in the AI Chip War
technology.excerpt: The San Diego chipmaker lands its first major data-centre ASIC customer — and thousands of Indian engineers in Hyderabad and Bangalore are at the centre of the pivot.
technology.image_caption: Closeup of electronic microchips on a circuit board — the kind of silicon at the centre of Qualcomm's new AI push. Photo: Pexels
technology.nri_angle: Qualcomm employs thousands of Indian chip designers in Hyderabad, Bangalore, and Chennai. This deal reshapes their career trajectory from mobile SoCs to cutting-edge AI inference silicon — and puts Indian engineering talent at the heart of the next chip battleground.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India's Tech Hubs Are Filing More Patents Than Ever. AI Is About to Accelerate That.
technology.excerpt: Global capability centres in Hyderabad, Bangalore, and Gurugram generated $98.4 billion in revenue last year — four years ahead of schedule. Now AI tools are turning them into IP factories.
technology.image_caption: Hyderabad's tech parks house some of the world's largest global capability centres. Photo: Pexels
technology.nri_angle: For NRIs weighing return-to-India decisions or considering investment in Indian tech, the GCC transformation signals that India's role is shifting from execution to invention. The patent surge means more senior, IP-generating roles — and higher salaries — in Indian tech hubs.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Salesforce's Agentforce Hit $1.2 Billion. Indian IT Services Should Be Worried.
technology.excerpt: The CRM giant beat earnings estimates but its AI agent platform threatens the consulting-heavy model that employs hundreds of thousands of Indians globally.
technology.image_caption: A modern tech workspace — the kind of environment where Salesforce's AI agents may soon replace human consultants.
technology.nri_angle: Salesforce is among the top H-1B employers in the US, and Indian IT services firms like TCS, Infosys, Wipro, and HCL derive billions from Salesforce consulting and implementation. The rise of Agentforce — AI agents that automate CRM workflows — directly threatens this labor-intensive model. For Indian-origin Salesforce developers, consultants, and IT services investors, this earnings report is a weather vane.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Marvell's AI Chip Bet Is Paying Off. Its India Engineers Are a Big Reason Why.
technology.excerpt: The semiconductor company posted record revenue and raised its outlook to $16.5 billion, powered by custom silicon that Indian design teams helped build.
technology.image_caption: A closeup of a microprocessor circuit board — the kind of custom silicon driving Marvell's AI-fueled growth.
technology.nri_angle: Marvell employs thousands of chip design engineers across Pune, Bangalore, and Hyderabad — the people literally designing the custom AI accelerators that hyperscalers are spending hundreds of billions on. For NRI semiconductor professionals and investors, this is a company where Indian talent directly drives the growth story.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India's AI Startups Raised $5 Billion in One Quarter. The Diaspora Is Watching.
technology.excerpt: A 73% funding surge, a $600 million sovereign AI bet, and Sarvam's potential unicorn status are reshaping India's claim to be more than just an AI talent exporter.
technology.image_caption: An abstract illustration of artificial intelligence — the technology powering India's fastest-growing startup category.
technology.nri_angle: For NRIs weighing return-to-India decisions or angel investments, India's AI funding surge signals that staying in Silicon Valley is no longer the only path to the AI frontier. Sovereign AI infrastructure (Neysa) and indigenous foundation models (Sarvam) are creating an ecosystem where Indian-origin AI researchers can build world-class companies at home — with Indian investors, Indian data, and Indian government backing.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Ramayana Part 1 Is Reportedly Coming a Week Before Diwali. The Cast List Alone Would Have Sold Out 2015.
entertainment.excerpt: Ranbir Kapoor as Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Sunny Deol as Hanuman. Music by AR Rahman and Hans Zimmer. Distribution deal: ₹450 crore. Release: October 30, 2026.
entertainment.image_caption: Ranbir Kapoor, who plays Lord Ram in Ramayana Part 1
entertainment.nri_angle: Ramayana is the most culturally significant Indian film project in a generation for the diaspora. The 1987 TV serial is a shared reference across NRI families worldwide. A big-screen adaptation with this cast and this budget, releasing during Diwali, will be the biggest Indian film event of the year in overseas markets.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Yash's Toxic Is the Most Expensive Kannada Film Ever Made. It Has Been Delayed Three Times. No One Knows When It Opens.
entertainment.excerpt: At ₹700-800 crore, Toxic was supposed to follow KGF into the stratosphere. Instead, it has bounced from March to June to a date yet to be announced.
entertainment.image_caption: Yash, star of KGF and the upcoming Toxic
entertainment.nri_angle: NRIs who packed theatres for KGF have been waiting for Yash's next. Toxic's repeated delays and enormous budget make it the biggest question mark in Indian cinema's global expansion — and the answer directly affects how many Kannada-language films get wide releases in North America and the UK.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: MasterChef India's First Winner Just Announced She Has Breast Cancer. She Left a 16-Year Teaching Career for This.
entertainment.excerpt: Pankaj Bhadouria, who won Season 1 in 2010 and became a household name for millions of NRI families, shared her diagnosis from a hospital bed on May 28.
entertainment.image_caption: Pankaj Bhadouria, winner of MasterChef India Season 1
entertainment.nri_angle: Bhadouria is a household name for NRI families who watched MasterChef India Season 1. Her diagnosis has sparked a health awareness conversation particularly relevant to South Asian women abroad, who consistently show lower breast cancer screening rates than the general population.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: June 2026 Might Be the Biggest Month in Indian Streaming History. Here's Everything Dropping.
entertainment.excerpt: Dhurandhar 2, Maa Behen, Gullak S5, Patriot, Bhooth Bangla, Raja Shivaji, and a Titan origin story — all in 30 days.
entertainment.image_caption: June 2026 brings an unprecedented wave of Indian content to streaming platforms worldwide
entertainment.nri_angle: For NRIs who rely on OTT for Indian content, June 2026 is the single richest month in streaming history — every major platform is dropping blockbuster titles simultaneously, eliminating the theatrical-to-digital wait that has long frustrated diaspora audiences.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Naseeruddin Shah Plays JRD Tata. Jim Sarbh Plays the Man He Trusted to Build Titan. It Drops June 3.
entertainment.excerpt: 'Made in India: A Titan Story' is a six-part Amazon MX Player series about how a watch company born in pre-liberalisation India became a global icon.
entertainment.image_caption: Naseeruddin Shah as JRD Tata in 'Made in India: A Titan Story', streaming free June 3 on Amazon MX Player
entertainment.nri_angle: Every NRI over 30 has a Titan memory — the watch their father wore, the Sonata from a school prize, the Fastrack bought with first pocket money. This series turns that shared experience into prestige television, free to stream worldwide.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: A 14-Year-Old From Haryana Just Beat Shah Rukh Khan on IMDb's Most Searched List. His Name Is Yudhvir Ahlawat.
entertainment.excerpt: The Kartavya actor topped IMDb India's weekly popularity rankings, surpassing Aishwarya Rai and CM Vijay. The streaming era just rewrote who gets to be famous.
entertainment.image_caption: Yudhvir Ahlawat's breakout performance in Netflix's Kartavya made him the most searched Indian actor on IMDb
entertainment.nri_angle: Ahlawat's rise proves that streaming has demolished the old gatekeeping system — a Hindi film about rural India now premieres simultaneously in 190 countries, and a teenager from Haryana can become a global search trend without ever leaving his hometown.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Marathi Cinema Just Had Its Best Month Ever. Two Films. ₹140 Crore. And Bollywood Watched.
entertainment.excerpt: Raja Shivaji broke Sairat's decade-old record. Deool Band 2 came from nowhere. May 2026 belongs to Maharashtra.
entertainment.nri_angle: Maharashtrian NRIs are driving strong overseas numbers for Raja Shivaji. The broader shift toward regional cinema dominating Hindi markets is reshaping what Indian films the diaspora sees on screens abroad.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Jr NTR Knelt at His Grandfather's Memorial. PM Modi Sent a Message. Chiranjeevi Said His Influence Will Never Fade.
entertainment.excerpt: N.T. Rama Rao would have turned 103. Three generations of Telugu cinema and politics stopped to remember why he still matters.
entertainment.nri_angle: NTR's mythological films were the cultural connective tissue for Telugu households abroad — his legacy is deeply personal for the Telugu diaspora and his grandson Jr NTR is now a global star.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Dhanush Made a ₹135 Crore Film About a Thief in 1990s Tamil Nadu. It Hit Netflix Today in Five Languages.
entertainment.excerpt: Kara flopped in theatres. On streaming, it might find the audience it was always meant for — including the NRI one.
entertainment.nri_angle: NRIs who missed Kara's theatrical run now have access in five languages on Netflix — the platform is increasingly becoming the primary way the diaspora watches new Indian cinema.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Sanjay Dutt Got the Idea for Khalnayak Returns in Prison. He Asked 4,000 Inmates to Write Him a One-Pager. Now He Can't Find a Director.
entertainment.excerpt: Rajkumar Santoshi politely declined. Subhash Ghai, who directed the 1993 original, already said no. Sanjay Dutt is still looking. The origin story of this sequel is wilder than any script.
entertainment.image_caption: Sanjay Dutt at the Khalnayak Returns announcement event in Mumbai
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Kangana Ranaut's Next Film Is About the Nurses Who Fought Back During 26/11. It Opens the Same Day as Imtiaz Ali's Partition Film.
entertainment.excerpt: Bharat Bhhagya Viddhaata releases June 12. Its motion poster focuses on hospital staff, security guards, and ordinary citizens who saved lives during the 2008 Mumbai attacks. The trailer title: 'The Unseen Heroes.'
entertainment.image_caption: Kangana Ranaut stars as a nurse in Bharat Bhhagya Viddhaata, a film about 26/11's unseen heroes
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Three Indian Titles Are on Netflix's Global Charts Right Now. Combined, They've Been Watched for 31 Million Hours.
entertainment.excerpt: Kartavya hit No. 1 on the Global Non-English Films list. Desi Bling is trending at No. 6 on Non-English TV. Dhurandhar: Raw and Undekha is at No. 5. At least one Indian title has charted every week since 2025.
entertainment.image_caption: Indian content is now a permanent fixture on Netflix's global charts
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: India Just Quarantined a Suspected Ebola Patient in Bengaluru. The US and Canada Have Banned Travellers From Three African Countries. Here Is What Every NRI Needs to Know.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The WHO has declared a global health emergency. India has launched airport screening. If you have family travelling between India and East Africa, the rules changed overnight.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Airport health screening measures have been activated across India and dozens of other countries in response to the Ebola outbreak
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Blood Test Can Now Screen You for Colon Cancer. The American Cancer Society Just Made It Official. South Asian Americans Have the Lowest Screening Rates in the Country.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The Guardant Shield test detects tumour DNA in your blood. One in three eligible Americans remain unscreened. For South Asians, that number may be three in four.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A simple blood draw can now screen for colorectal cancer under updated ACS guidelines. | Pexels
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: America Just Declared Your Child's Screen Time a Public Health Crisis. The Recommended Limit for Teenagers Is Two Hours a Day. Most Indian-American Kids Are Doing Double That.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new Surgeon General's advisory calls for bell-to-bell phone bans in schools, age-gated design changes from tech companies, and family media plans. For Indian-American parents who grew up without screens, the rules of engagement just changed.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A 19-Year Study of 20,000 Adults Found That the Type of Sitting Matters More Than the Amount. Mentally Active Sitting Cuts Dementia Risk. Passive Sitting Raises It.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Researchers tracked sedentary behaviour for nearly two decades and found that replacing one hour of TV-watching with reading or puzzles was associated with a significant reduction in dementia risk. For Indian tech workers who sit 10 hours a day and come home to Netflix, the distinction is not academic.

sources.label: Frontiers in Public Health — Sedentary Behaviour and Burnout

lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Asian Americans Have the Lowest Rate of Anxiety Medication Use in the Country. A National Study of 29,000 Adults Found That Cultural Stigma Is Only Part of the Explanation.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A May 2026 Frontiers study found that even after controlling for income, insurance, and education, Asian adults had 45 per cent lower odds of taking anxiety medication than White adults. For South Asian families where mental health is still discussed in whispers, the treatment gap is likely even wider.

sources.label: Emory University — South Asian Women Mental Health

lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Study of 100,000 People Found That Food Dyes Raise Diabetes Risk by 38 Per Cent and Cancer Risk by 14 Per Cent. Your Grandmother's Kitchen Did Not Use a Single One of Them.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The NutriNet-Santé cohort study is the first to link colour additives to chronic disease at scale. Curcumin as an additive — not as turmeric — was the worst offender.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Turmeric in whole-food form offers anti-inflammatory benefits. As an isolated food additive, it was linked to a 49 per cent increase in diabetes risk.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Diabetes Drug Millions of South Asians Already Take May Be Quietly Slowing Their Cancer. A Cleveland Clinic Study of 12,112 Patients Found the Evidence.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic cut cancer progression by up to 55 per cent across four tumour types. South Asians, who carry the world's highest diabetes burden, may be benefiting without knowing it.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: GLP-1 receptor agonists, originally developed for diabetes, are showing unexpected cancer-protective properties
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Study of 17,000 Adults Found You Need Four Times More Exercise Than the Guidelines Recommend. The 150-Minute Rule Is a Floor, Not a Ceiling.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Researchers at Macao Polytechnic University found that 560 to 610 minutes of weekly aerobic exercise — about 85 minutes a day — reduced cardiovascular events by more than 30 per cent. The standard 150-minute guideline cut risk by only 8 per cent.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The American Heart Association Just Rewrote Its Dietary Rules. Your Mother's Indian Kitchen Already Follows Most of Them.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The 2026 AHA guidelines prioritise plant proteins over meat, push potassium and whole grains, and take a harder line on alcohol. Traditional Indian cooking checks nearly every box — except the one about salt.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Parents' Three-Meals-a-Day Habit Was Protecting Their Muscles. A Study Found That Eating Fewer Than Three Meals Is Independently Linked to Lower Muscle Mass — Regardless of How Much Protein You Eat.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The Korean study adds to mounting evidence that meal frequency matters as much as total intake for preserving skeletal muscle. For Indian families watching their elders skip meals to manage blood sugar, the implications are urgent.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Sixty-One Per Cent of Asian Adults With Type 2 Diabetes Already Show Early Muscle Loss. South Asians Are the Most Vulnerable Group. Your Parents May Not Know They Have It.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new meta-analysis of 14 studies across Asia found that sarcopenia begins years before diabetes patients notice it — and the vegetarian diets many Indian families follow may be accelerating the decline.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: One Hour of Recovery Sleep After a Bad Night Erases the Mortality Signal. A Study of 574,000 Nights Proves Your Body Knows What It Needs — If You Let It.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Tsinghua University researchers tracked 85,000 people with wrist-worn devices. Those who slept one extra hour after sleep deprivation had the same mortality risk as those who never lost sleep at all.

sources.label: Dr. Jean-Philippe Chaput, University of Ottawa

lifestyle-health.nri_angle: NRI professionals routinely grind through sleep-deprived weekdays with no recovery signal. This study shows the body can self-repair after a bad night — but only if the alarm clock and caffeine do not override it.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk
